title_support.candidate_title: Rainfall-associated expansion of frog active communities is more boundary-biased than uniform activation predicts

interpretation: The observed four-component allocation remains strongly inconsistent with uniform activation even when the null uses cell-only historical frequencies and strongly anchors each pair to its observed dry species x stop state. The result therefore cannot be attributed simply to hierarchical shrinkage weakening persistent species x stop identity.
ecological_hypothesis_boundary: Preferential recruitment of combinations rare in dry conditions, including temporary or intermittently suitable wet sites, is a plausible discussion-level explanation only; no unique mechanism or causal rainfall effect is identified.
